pass_a_gloss: Isa 28:9-11 applied to Ambrose and Protoctetus as weaned athletes: affliction-upon-affliction then hope-upon-hope.
pass_b_english: "Those weaned from milk, drawn from the breast: affliction upon affliction expect; hope upon hope expect; yet a little, yet a little — through contempt of lips, through another tongue." (Isaiah 28:9–11) And you, then — after Isaiah — as no longer carnal nor babes 'in Christ,' advanced 'in' your intelligible 'stature,' most godly Ambrose and most pious Protoctetus, no longer 'having need of milk' but of 'solid food' — hear, as 'weaned from milk' and 'drawn from the breast,' in what way, as for weaned athletes, no simple affliction but an 'affliction upon affliction' is prophesied. He who does not push away the affliction 'upon affliction,' but as a noble athlete 'expects' it, straightway expects 'hope upon hope' too — which, after a little of the affliction 'upon affliction,' he shall enjoy. For such is the 'yet a little, yet a little.' (1 Corinthians 3:1) (Hebrews 5:12) (Luke 2:52)
